paragraphs.text: Shipment NOG-10-01 occurred at Nogales, Sonora on 2010-06-15. A bar owner in contact with the reporting office described a convoy of produce trucks staging on the Sonora side of the Nogales crossing late at night, which the owner took to be a smuggling run. On questioning, the owner acknowledged that produce trucks routinely stage overnight to be first in the commercial lanes at dawn and could not point to anything specific about this convoy. The reporting office treats the account as a description of ordinary crossing traffic.

The owner described the general atmosphere in the border district as tense following a dispute between two local crews over who could charge fees on the truck lots. The owner did not know the names of the crews and stated that the dispute had not produced violence. The owner mentioned that drivers complained of longer waits at the commercial crossing and that some had begun using the crossing at San Luis Río Colorado instead. The owner added that the truck lots on the Sonora side are owned by a handful of families and that whoever collects the fees on those lots effectively decides which drivers reach the lanes first. The owner believes the dispute began when one family raised its fee without consulting the other.

The reporting office assesses this as background on the crossing environment. The source's access is limited to conversations with drivers and truck lot staff. This reporting is consistent with the pattern of activity observed on the corridor in prior months. The reporting office will continue to collect on the truck lot dispute as a possible indicator of a change in control at the crossing.
